assessments.reasoning: Once OrdinaryGet has an own accessor descriptor, an undefined getter yields undefined. Otherwise it passes the getter and Receiver to Call. The additional §7.3.13 passage establishes that Call forwards its second argument as the this argument.

challenge.method: Use a Receiver distinct from the descriptor owner and trace both a missing getter and a throwing getter.
challenge.results: The missing getter exits before Call. For a present getter the original Receiver reaches [[Call]], and a thrown completion propagates. Own data properties and missing descriptors leave through earlier branches.

limitations: This concerns the accessor branch. The separate data, missing descriptor, and other internal-method algorithms have their own rules. A getter call can throw.
The conclusion concerns the this argument passed into [[Call]]. The function's own this-binding semantics govern what its body observes, and its call can complete abruptly.
